entities.summary: Jerónimo Xavierre was a Spanish Dominican theologian born in Zaragoza in 1546 and died in 1608. He played a key role in the Spanish Inquisition, serving as an inquisitor in Toledo, where he interrogated and condemned numerous heretics. Xavierre's writings on the nature of the Holy Spirit and the sacraments were influential in the Counter-Reformation, contributing to the Catholic Church's efforts to suppress Protestantism in Europe. His work also had a lasting impact on the development of Catholic doctrine and the treatment of heretics in the Spanish Empire.
